label: Unit 2
intro: A sensor notices; a motor moves. Put a visible block in the pretend robot path and give it a rule before it starts. Then move the same toy load with a ramp or lever and ask where the push came from.

gelds.text: Sensor cue, human rule and motor action
Ramps, levers and wheels moved by hand
Choosing a machine while keeping the decision with a person

tryNote: Use a toy load, a board ramp and a ruler balanced on a block. Keep loads light enough to move with one finger.

daily.title: Block means stop
daily.do: Say the robot rule: stop when you see a block. Walk toward a block together and stop. Ask what he noticed.
daily.stretch: Change the rule to turn left at the block; he predicts the move and explains the cue, the person who chose the rule and the motor that would move a real robot.

daily.title: Move the same load
daily.do: Push a toy car up a low board ramp, then lift a light block with a ruler lever. He names the tool. Keep the load the same when comparing.
daily.stretch: He explains how the ramp, lever or wheels helped, chooses one for moving that load again, and says whose hand supplied the push instead of a battery.
daily.skill: Simple machines and the source of motion

daily.title: Plan, then check
daily.do: Say a short robot route before trying it. When the toy will not move, check its power, switch and path in that order with a grown-up. The toy stays closed.
daily.stretch: Plan four or five directions before Run, then explain which machine could repeat that trip and which destination a person still needs to choose.

goalsTitle: What he should have by the end of this unit

his: Explains how battery, switch, sensor, and motor each help a powered robot notice and move.
Predicts a pretend robot's action from a visible sensor cue and a stated human instruction.
Plans a four- or five-step robot route before Run and checks power, switch, then obstacles when a toy will not move.
Names a ramp, lever, and wheel and demonstrates how one helps move a toy load without needing its own battery.
Chooses a suitable machine for a repeated moving job and explains which decision still belongs to a person.

weekend: Set up a small delivery route for blocks. He chooses a ramp or wheeled toy, gives the pretend sensor a rule, and explains which decisions you made before anything moved.

songs.title: Notice, Then Go
songs.style: Start singing immediately, with no instrumental intro. Bouncy plucked bass, light drums and woodblocks with a steady walking beat. One clear warm voice, short repeated melody, steady preschool pace, clean ending without a long outro.
lyrics: Follow the rule the person chose.
Roll the load, lift it slow.
Simple tools help make it go.
See the block and stop right there.
Turn when told, leave room to spare.
Switch turns on; the job's begun.
Ramp and lever, wheel that rolls,
Hands can push toward our goals.
Follow the rule the person chose.

lines.start: Tell the robot how to get to the battery.
lines.wall: The robot bumped into something. Fix your program and try again.
lines.stop: The robot stopped in the wrong place. Fix your program and try again.
lines.win: Your robot made it to the battery!

basic.label: Battery
basic.note: A battery supplies power to a battery toy.

basic.label: Switch
basic.note: The switch lets you turn the toy on or off.

basic.label: Wheel
basic.note: A wheel rolls as the toy moves.

basic.label: Robot
basic.note: A person gives a robot instructions for its job.

basic.label: Block
basic.note: A block can be an obstacle in the robot path.

basic.label: Hand
basic.note: Your hand supplies the push for a hand-powered toy.

advanced.label: Sensor
advanced.note: A sensor detects something such as light or an obstacle.

advanced.label: Motor
advanced.note: A motor uses power to make a part move.

advanced.label: Ramp
advanced.note: A ramp gives a load a sloping path up or down.

advanced.label: Lever
advanced.note: A spoon can act as a lever when it pivots on a support.

advanced.label: Pulley
advanced.note: A pulley guides a rope over a wheel to help move a load.

advanced.label: Camera
advanced.note: A camera sensor captures light to make a picture.

advanced.label: Light
advanced.note: A light can be the visible cue in a robot rule.

advanced.label: Load
advanced.note: The load is the thing the machine moves.

items.text: The robot sensor detects a block ahead.
items.note: The sensor is noticing the block.

items.text: The robot wheels roll forward.
items.note: Rolling wheels move the robot.

items.text: The camera detects light from the window.
items.note: The camera is sensing light.

items.text: The motor turns the toy arm.
items.note: Turning the arm is movement.

items.text: The touch sensor detects your finger.
items.note: The sensor notices the touch.

items.text: The robot gripper lifts a block.
items.note: The gripper moves the block upward.

items.text: The microphone detects a clap.
items.note: The microphone senses sound.

items.text: The robot drives left.
items.note: Driving changes the robot position.

items.text: The sensor detects a dark line on the floor.
items.note: The line is information the sensor notices.

items.text: The wheels are still while the sensor detects a nearby box.
items.note: The robot can notice something while its wheels stay still.

items.text: After the sensor finds a box, the arm lifts it; sort the lifting.
items.note: The lifting part moves the box.

items.text: The robot rolls while its camera detects a red card; sort the detecting.
items.note: The camera sensing and wheels moving are different jobs.

items.text: A person pushes the robot with its power off; sort the rolling.
items.note: It is movement even though a hand supplies the push.

items.text: A motor turns the camera toward the door; sort the turning.
items.note: Turning the camera is movement, before its next picture.

items.text: A toy car drives using its battery.
items.note: The battery supplies the car power.

items.text: Your hand pushes a wooden car.
items.note: Your hand supplies the push.

items.text: A battery fan spins its blades.
items.note: The fan motor uses battery power.

items.text: Your hand lifts a toy load with a ruler lever.
items.note: Your hand pushes the lever.

items.text: A battery robot walks across the mat.
items.note: Its motors use the battery power.

items.text: You pull a rope over a pulley to lift a block.
items.note: You supply the pull on the rope.

items.text: A battery train drives around its track.
items.note: The train uses battery power to move.

items.text: You push a toy box up a ramp.
items.note: The ramp has no battery; you push the box.

items.text: A battery screwdriver turns a screw.
items.note: The motor uses battery power to turn.

items.text: The robot battery is removed and you push it by hand.
items.note: This movement comes from your hand, not a battery.

items.text: A battery motor pulls the rope over a pulley.
items.note: The pulley helps, but the battery motor supplies this pull.

items.text: You turn a screwdriver with your wrist.
items.note: This screwdriver uses the turn of your hand.

items.text: A battery car drives up a wooden ramp.
items.note: The ramp has no battery, but the car does.

items.text: You turn a toy crank that lifts a load with no battery attached.
items.note: Your hand powers the crank and the lift.

steps.text: Say stop when the sensor sees a block
Put it in the wheeled toy
Put the light load on one end
Press the other end to lift it
Stop trying to run the toy
Ask Dad to check the power
Clear the obstacle in the path
Push the load up the ramp
Say how the ramp helped your hand
Put a visible block beside the route
Give the rule to stop when the sensor sees the block
Run the route and follow the stop rule
